positions.summary_short: Rick Maloney seeks re-election on responsible growth, affordability, housing, health care, infrastructure and environmental stewardship.
summary_bullets: Incumbent mayor seeking re-election on a platform of putting residents first and managing growth responsibly.
Priorities listed: affordability, housing, health care, infrastructure, economic opportunity, environmental stewardship and quality of life.
Promises experienced, steady, responsible leadership; says Bracebridge can keep growing and investing without losing sight of who it is.
positions.verbatim_quote: My commitment is to continue providing experienced, steady and responsible leadership while keeping a clear focus on affordability, housing, health care, infrastructure, economic opportunity, environmental stewardship and the quality of life for all our residents.
positions.source_title: Meet the Candidates (Certified) - Town of Bracebridge official election page

positions.summary_short: Rick Maloney backs the physician-supported Stage 1.3 hospital model with 46 beds, supports obstetrics, and says the town's $10-million pledge is conditional.
summary_bullets: Supports the physician-supported Stage 1.3 model (46 inpatient beds and 27 emergency-department spaces in Bracebridge) rather than a fixed 60-bed target.
Says equitable access means appropriate care regardless of where people live, not identical services at both sites.
Strongly supports obstetrical services at the future South Muskoka hospital and restoring currently suspended services when staffing permits.
Town's $10-million contribution is conditional and capped; council can reconsider if the project scope changes.
Opposes pushing South Muskoka to the back of the line for a new hospital given 50+ other municipalities are also advocating.
positions.verbatim_quote: I strongly support obstetrical services at the future South Muskoka hospital. MAHC has assured the Town that Stage 1.3 includes an obstetrical unit in Bracebridge.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Bracebridge

positions.summary_short: Norman Raynor wants a bigger South Muskoka hospital than MAHC's plan, restored obstetrics and ALC beds, and opposes the Pine Street site.
summary_bullets: Wants MORE than 60 acute-care beds at the future South Muskoka hospital, citing a billion-dollar budget and lower-cost comparator builds.
Wants MAHC to restore obstetrics and ALC beds at South Muskoka Memorial; calls hospital management Huntsville-focused.
Does not support the Pine Street site, which he says the Town selected from Fowler Construction; wants the hospital to stay where it is or be properly justified.
Will not support paying the same amount as Huntsville for less hospital; demands cost per bed and per service calculations.
If elected, would demand a more equitable plan from MAHC, contact the Minister of Health, and coordinate with other South Muskoka municipalities.
positions.verbatim_quote: I will fight to get the best possible hospital for Bracebridge. I will have regular discussions with MAHC to restore services such as obstetrics, and ALC beds to our hospital.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Bracebridge

positions.summary_short: Norman Raynor pledges zero tax increases, leaner overlapping government, and open meetings.
summary_bullets: Pledges no tax increases and would trim budgets to achieve a zero tax increase, supporting needs not wants.
Opposes the District building a $17 million factory; says there is too much overlap of District and Town responsibilities, especially roads.
Would give local contractors that hire local workers priority in Town contract awards.
Against closed-door meetings; would start a regular paper newsletter since not everyone uses the internet.
positions.verbatim_quote: I will work to make sure we have no tax increases. I will trim budgets if need be to achieve a zero tax increase. I will only support needs not wants.
positions.source_title: Meet the Candidates (Certified) - Town of Bracebridge official election page

positions.summary_short: Christian McEachran Morin wants at least 60 beds, prefers two self-sustaining hospitals, and withholds judgment on the MAHC model until the transport plan is complete.
summary_bullets: Supports advocating for a minimum of 60 acute-care beds; does not see how fewer beds serve a larger population.
Concerned about the transportation plan between sites; would prefer two self-sustaining hospitals in Muskoka.
Undecided on obstetrics, defers to health professionals and mothers while leaning toward keeping the service.
Would not commit municipal taxpayer money until the plan satisfies all of Muskoka's taxpayers.
Undecided on the current MAHC model until the transportation plan is worked out.
positions.verbatim_quote: I am concerned about the transportation plan and would prefer to see 2 self-sustaining hospitals in Muskoka.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Bracebridge

positions.summary_short: Christian McEachran Morin campaigns on climate accountability, citing his successful push for a District climate reserve fund in 2023.
summary_bullets: In 2023 attended District Committee of the Whole as a member of the public to demand a reserve fund for the MCCAP climate plan; councillors passed the motion.
Opposes paving over forests and wetlands for subdivisions, garbage on roads and waterways, and warns of increased flooding and heatwaves.
Campaign signs are secondhand and repurposed as part of the circular economy instead of single-use plastic signs.
positions.verbatim_quote: I believe in protecting Muskoka's natural environment, and in 2020, District Council approved the MCCAP to do just that. Yet, by 2023, they still had not set up a reserve fund to pay for the ambitious projects they wanted to complete, so I stood up to ask why.
positions.source_title: votecmm.ca - Christian McEachran Morin District Council 2026-2030

positions.summary_short: Christian McEachran Morin wants an elected District Chair and follow-through on existing municipal plans.
summary_bullets: Says party politics do not belong in municipal governance.
Argues the District Chair should be an elected position; criticizes the province for quashing the elected chair in 2018 and legislating appointment in 2026.
Wants to move forward with existing plans so residents see results, not just talk.
positions.verbatim_quote: Party politics don't belong in municipal governance. The District Chair should be an elected position, but in 2018, the conservative provincial government quashed that and in 2026 they've passed legislation to appoint the District Chair.
positions.source_title: votecmm.ca - Christian McEachran Morin District Council 2026-2030

positions.summary_short: Christian McEachran Morin wants infrastructure that keeps pace with growth, including active transportation and a vibrant downtown.
summary_bullets: Says Bracebridge infrastructure must reflect future needs: expanded public and active transportation options.
Wants parks, schools and amenities near new subdivisions, and a focus on a vibrant downtown.
positions.verbatim_quote: Bracebridge is a growing community and we need to make sure our infrastructure reflects the needs of the future.
positions.source_title: votecmm.ca - Christian McEachran Morin District Council 2026-2030

positions.summary_short: Brenda Rhodes backs the physician-supported Stage 1.3 model and the town's conditional $10-million hospital contribution.
summary_bullets: Supports the physicians' conclusion that 46 acute-care beds and 27 emergency beds in Bracebridge would work; planning uses provincial bed formulas.
Strongly supports obstetrics at the South Muskoka site, says MAHC assured an obstetrical unit plus a specialized women's clinic.
Town's $10 million contribution helped secure major provincial investment; should be revisited only if the scope changes substantively.
Fully supports the one hospital, two sites model, citing innovation like virtual care and flexible facilities.
positions.verbatim_quote: I fully support the one hospital, two sites model. It creates exciting opportunities for services we don't have today and invites new, innovative ways of working.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Bracebridge

positions.summary_short: Brenda Rhodes seeks re-election on responsible growth, healthy finances, environmental protection, affordability and housing.
summary_bullets: Incumbent Deputy Mayor and Town/District Councillor of four years, describes her approach as steady, thoughtful local government.
Keeping the community kind and connected means responsible growth, healthy finances, real environmental protection, affordability, housing and health care that reaches beyond the hospital.
Emphasizes communication: returning calls, showing up, and explaining the why behind votes with a view to future councils and generations.
positions.verbatim_quote: Good local government isn't flashy - it's steady and thoughtful: showing up, listening, and making decisions that hold up ten years from now, not just until the next election.
positions.source_title: Meet the Candidates (Certified) - Town of Bracebridge official election page

positions.summary_short: Don Smith supports at least 60 beds and local care, but wants the Province's position on Stage 1.3 before judging the model.
summary_bullets: Supports advocating for a minimum of 60 acute-care beds but wants clarity first on the Province's position on the Stage 1.3 submission and each site's share of investment.
Believes acute care should be delivered locally whenever possible so families can support patients.
Continued the advocacy that saw obstetrics included in the hospital's 1.3 submission.
Says the community deserves more information before any funds are advanced; neither the Town nor the District took a blank-cheque approach.
Undecided on the current model until the Province's position on Stage 1.3 is known.
positions.verbatim_quote: From my perspective, it is important to see the Province's position on the hospital's Stage 1.3 submission and the future unfolding of plans before any funds are advanced.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Bracebridge

positions.summary_short: Don Smith's priorities include affordable housing, healthcare including mental health, a smaller District Council, and waterfront access.
summary_bullets: Priorities: continuing gains in affordable housing, better healthcare with attention to mental health, a positive local business environment.
Wants to reduce the size of District Council, modernize municipal operations, and implement more public waterfront access.
Says the watershed and environment deserve attention at both council tables.
positions.verbatim_quote: Listening to you and giving a voice to your concerns at both the Town and District Council tables are the two commitments I have made since first being elected.
positions.source_title: Meet the Candidates (Certified) - Town of Bracebridge official election page

positions.summary_short: Tatiana Sutherland supports at least 60 beds and local obstetrics, and ties any municipal funding to clear evidence of equitable capacity.
summary_bullets: Supports a minimum of 60 acute-care beds, provided the capacity is supported by utilization data and credible projections.
Supports maintaining obstetrical services with the staffing and resources for safe, reliable maternity care.
Would not commit municipal taxpayer funding without clear evidence the plan provides equitable capacity for South Muskoka.
Position is constructive engagement and continued scrutiny; not yet satisfied the model ensures equitable access.
positions.verbatim_quote: Supporting our hospitals and protecting the interests of municipal taxpayers are not competing responsibilities. We have an obligation to do both.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Bracebridge

positions.summary_short: Tatiana Sutherland campaigns on environmental protection, attainable housing and local health care.
summary_bullets: Focuses on protecting Muskoka's environment, creating more attainable housing, and strengthening local health care.
Chair of the Muskoka Community Land Trust, working on practical housing solutions.
Works in Muskoka's tourism sector, which supports many local families and businesses.
positions.verbatim_quote: Over the past four years, I have focused on the issues I believe matter deeply to our future - protecting Muskoka's environment, creating more attainable housing and strengthening local health care.
positions.source_title: Meet the Candidates (Certified) - Town of Bracebridge official election page

positions.summary_short: Brian Koehn focuses on roads, parking, garbage and recycling, and supporting local businesses.
summary_bullets: Wants to focus on better roads, parking, and improving garbage and recycling services.
Supports local businesses; above all wants to listen to residents and make sure their concerns are heard.
positions.verbatim_quote: Id like to focus on better roads, parking, supporting local businesses, and improving garbage and recycling services.
positions.source_title: Meet the Candidates (Certified) - Town of Bracebridge official election page

positions.summary_short: Debbie Vernon pledges accessible, responsive leadership focused on responsible spending, environment and affordable housing.
summary_bullets: Pledges to be accessible, listening, and responsive to ideas, concerns and queries around municipal affairs.
Wants tax dollars managed responsibly; a healthy environment is a healthy economy.
Says building community capacity to plan differently for ALC beds and affordable housing is needed; wants collaboration with community, Indigenous people and the province.
positions.verbatim_quote: Building community capacity to plan differently for ALC beds and affordable housing is needed.
positions.source_title: Meet the Candidates (Certified) - Town of Bracebridge official election page

positions.summary_short: Debbie Vernon's campaign emphasizes environmental advocacy for Muskoka's lakes.
summary_bullets: Campaign highlights her local expertise and environmental advocacy.
Endorsed in a testimonial by Friends of the Muskoka Watershed for hard work, commitment and vision on lakes and the environment.
positions.verbatim_quote: The Friends of the Muskoka Watershed wouldn't be where it is today without Debbie Vernon's hard work, commitment and vision.
positions.source_title: Elect Debbie Vernon for Councillor - testimonials

positions.summary_short: Donna Kearney wants obstetrics restored and the hospital site re-examined, and supports 46 beds only if primary care and ALC are addressed.
summary_bullets: Firmly believes obstetrics must be available in South Muskoka, potentially led by Muskoka midwives, to attract younger people.
Concerned the Pine Street site on the highway would serve external populations more than locals; prefers the Fife Farm site for walkability and nearby staff housing.
Says 46 beds may be adequate if primary care access (12,000 without providers) and ALC rates are fixed through community partnerships.
Would bring location and obstetrics back to the table before supporting the rest of the redevelopment plan.
positions.verbatim_quote: We need to attract younger people to south Muskoka, which aligns with Town planning, so obstetrics must be available.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Bracebridge

positions.summary_short: Donna Kearney pledges accessible public engagement and follow-through with Macaulay Ward residents.
summary_bullets: Pledges public engagement opportunities in Macaulay Ward so she is easily accessible.
Says staying connected matters because opinions and priorities change over time.
Believes follow-through preserves trust; once trust is lost a councillor is no longer effective.
positions.verbatim_quote: It will be my intention, if elected to council, to hold public engagement opportunities in Macaulay Ward so I am easily accessible.
positions.source_title: Donna Kearney - MSM Connect 2026 Municipal Election Candidate Spotlight

positions.summary_short: Donna Kearney wants a thriving year-round economy, expanded green spaces and safe active transportation.
summary_bullets: Believes in fair and equitable access to the basics of life: food, shelter and safety.
Supports a thriving year-round economy, expanding green spaces, and safe active transportation for all ages.
Frames environmental, economic, social and population health as one healthy community to invest in.
positions.verbatim_quote: I believe in expanding green spaces to highlight the natural beauty of the area and in creating safe spaces for active transportation to promote healthy lifestyles for all ages.
positions.source_title: Meet the Candidates (Certified) - Town of Bracebridge official election page

positions.summary_short: Andrew Struthers wants taxes held at or below inflation, transparent long-term forecasts, and growth to pay for growth.
summary_bullets: Wants tax increases held at or below inflation even through major capital projects, measured against the 8-year average.
Demands full transparency on long-term multi-year forecasts, not budget-by-budget.
Wants growth to pay for growth: development charge relief paired with real fiscal guardrails.
positions.verbatim_quote: Hold the line on the 8-year average - keep tax increases as close to or below inflation as fiscally responsible, even through major capital projects.
positions.source_title: Meet the Candidates (Certified) - Town of Bracebridge official election page

positions.summary_short: Andrew Struthers defers to South Muskoka doctors on hospital capacity, demands obstetrics locally, and ties funding to doctors' support.
summary_bullets: Stands 100% behind South Muskoka doctors on bed numbers: if doctors support 46 beds he will not argue.
Obstetrical care must be at every hospital; South Muskoka babies should be born in South Muskoka.
Only supported municipal contributions after doctors supported the plan; would change his mind if doctors gave different information.
Undecided on the model pending an updated doctors' position and an independent peer review of financials and engineering.
positions.verbatim_quote: Obstetrical care must be at every hospital. South Muskoka babies should be born in South Muskoka.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Bracebridge

positions.summary_short: Andrew Struthers wants the Memorial Arena housing redevelopment delivered on time and on budget.
summary_bullets: Wants delivery on housing commitments: Memorial Arena site redevelopment, on time and on budget.
Backs the Community Safety and Well-Being Plan with real follow-through at the Town level.
positions.verbatim_quote: Deliver on housing commitments - Memorial Arena site redevelopment, on time and on budget.
positions.source_title: Meet the Candidates (Certified) - Town of Bracebridge official election page

positions.summary_short: Laura Craig focuses on road maintenance, fair investment in Draper Ward and stronger local healthcare.
summary_bullets: Would advocate for improved road maintenance and fair investment in Draper Ward.
Wants stronger local healthcare services.
Describes herself as a small business owner, not a career politician, bringing a practical, honest approach.
positions.verbatim_quote: As your councillor, I will advocate for improved road maintenance, fair investment in Draper Ward, and stronger local healthcare services.
positions.source_title: Meet the Candidates (Certified) - Town of Bracebridge official election page

positions.summary_short: Cindy Waters opposes the MAHC redevelopment model and wants the board dissolved, backed by her 14,000-signature Care Close to Home petition.
summary_bullets: Does not support the current MAHC redevelopment model; says it does not improve on what exists now and has no obstetrics.
Believes the MAHC board needs to be dissolved and returned to two boards; wants the province to review how the board is selected.
Led a petition with more than 14,000 signatures and asked the province to let democracy prevail in decision-making.
Opposes the Pine Street site (gravel pit remediation, fire service questions) and any municipal funding for a plan with no OB and no Care Close to Home beds.
positions.verbatim_quote: I continue to believe the Board needs to be dissolved to return to 2 Boards.
positions.source_title: SSMHC 2026 Municipal Candidate Questionnaire Results - Bracebridge

positions.summary_short: Cindy Waters pledges accountability, taxpayer value and responsible growth that protects Draper's rural character.
summary_bullets: Will ask the hard questions, look carefully at the numbers, and support decisions that provide value for taxpayers.
Growth must be responsible and supported by infrastructure and services.
Wants to protect Bracebridge's character, rural communities, waterways and natural environment while supporting responsible economic development and housing.
positions.verbatim_quote: I will ask the hard questions, look carefully at the numbers and support decisions that provide value for taxpayers.
positions.source_title: Meet the Candidates (Certified) - Town of Bracebridge official election page

positions.summary_short: Sandy Inkster promises collaboration, listening and compassionate action as TLDSB trustee.
summary_bullets: Committed to connecting and collaborating: learning about the partners, the roles and building relationships.
Listening and speaking: giving space for all voices, being available to listen and taking a turn to have a voice.
Taking action with compassion: honouring the progressive TLDSB by following through, with compassion during challenging times.
positions.verbatim_quote: Taking Action with Compassion - continuing to honour the progressive TLDSB by following through, by having compassion for the partners during the process, especially during challenging times.
positions.source_title: Meet the Candidates (Certified) - Town of Bracebridge official election page

positions.summary_short: Richard Struthers sees the trustee role as communication and access for schools and parents, backed by 40 years in manufacturing leadership.
summary_bullets: Says the role of trustee is to provide communication and access on behalf of schools and parents.
Brings forty years as CEO of a manufacturing company, including 15 years in Bracebridge, understanding finance, administration and management.
positions.verbatim_quote: The role of trustee to is provide communication and access of behalf of our schools and parents.
positions.source_title: Meet the Candidates (Certified) - Town of Bracebridge official election page

positions.summary_short: Donald Blais prioritizes child well-being, safe schools, belonging and graduation rates.
summary_bullets: Top concern is the well-being of children: a safe school, tools and training for staff, and a sense of belonging for families regardless of background, beliefs or orientation.
Supports the Committee for Children in Difficulty with the necessary budget.
Wants high graduation rates by helping children reach their full potential.
positions.verbatim_quote: Provide all the necessary tools and training to staff members to maintain a safe environment in our schools.
positions.source_title: Vote Donald Blais: School Trustee - votedonaldblais.ca

positions.summary_short: Donald Blais promises transparency and leans on 12 years as trustee and relationships with officials.
summary_bullets: Wants transparency: minimize closed-door discussions and maximize public debates.
Cites 12 years as a school trustee and good relations with provincial politicians, the Director of Education, superintendents and staff.
Supports traditional professions promotion to address AI labour-market changes and environmental education.
positions.verbatim_quote: Minimize closed-door discussions and maximize public debates.
positions.source_title: Vote Donald Blais: School Trustee - votedonaldblais.ca
